answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can influence market decisions; the protocol slashes that stake when independently sampled tasks expose fabricated work. One operator can still create many identities, but each needs its own locked capital, and a detected fake loses it, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free. The island market can place a new agent on a low-impact ledge until it earns a glacier of verified history, limiting damage while evidence accumulates.
